programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo reaches the jet age in the Derby suburb of Peartree, where he tours the engineering colossus Rolls-Royce. In Derby city centre, Michael is on the trail of little-known modernist sculptor Ronald Pope, admiring two of his works and discovering how Pope began his working life as an engineer at Rolls-Royce. The chance to catapult a model train along a 150-metre-long track into a purpose-built wind tunnel takes Michael to Derby's Railway Technical Centre, founded in 1967 and once the largest railway research complex in the world. Michael’s last stop is Nottingham, where he finds one of the oldest bicycle companies in the world, Raleigh, and discovers how a bold, new idea became a craze.

programme.title: Walking With...
programme.desc: Steph McGovern walks along the charming and isolated valley of Littondale in the heart of the Yorkshire Dales, describing her special connection with the area. From the hamlet of Foxup she makes her way along roads and riverside paths to the capital of the dale at Arncliffe. Walking alone with a just a 360-degree camera, she meets farmers who have been on this land for generations and youngsters who are starting a new business. Following the course of the River Skirfare, her path passes farmhouses and through the village of Litton. Steph relishes the chance to ‘get off the treadmill’ and takes a moment to hear the flow of the water and smell the flowers. Steph describes how the dales have always had a place in her heart – they are landscapes she returns to in difficult times. Along the way she expresses thoughts on fame and family.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: An AI-generated actor called Tilly Norwood has been cast in the lead role of a forthcoming film, adding to the debate about artificial intelligence in filmmaking. The announcement follows criticism from actors such as Emily Blunt, and objections from the US performers' union. Eline Van der Velden, founder and CEO of Particle6, explains why she created Tilly Norwood, while Jake Kanter, international investigations editor at Deadline, sets out the reaction from the film industry. Andy Burnham has become the UK's new prime minister, and his approach to the media is already attracting attention. His team has relied more on social media, online creators and direct communication than on traditional broadcast interviews. Lizzy Buchan, political editor of the Daily Mirror; Jennifer Gerber, senior political advisor, WA Communications; Tom Nicholas, creator of the Slow News Day YouTube channel; and broadcaster Andrew Neil, presenter of The Andrew Neil Report, assess what this could mean for political journalism and public accountability.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: There’s growing concern for Malaika, the elderly lioness, whose health has been deteriorating. The keepers and vets decide that their only option is to sedate her to find out what’s been troubling her, but knocking out any animal, especially an elderly one, is a risk. At nearly 20 years old, she now faces a fresh diagnosis, but will they be able to get this wily old girl to take the medication that could help her? Meanwhile, there’s cause for celebration in Animal Adventure, where red squirrel parents Rory and Pinecone have had a litter of elusive new kittens – Megan checks in with keeper Chris to find out how they’re getting on. Also, Kate and Ben join forces to help carry out vital health checks on Red, the largest Amur tiger at the park. It’s essential keepers continually assess his fitness and health, but when you’re dealing with a tiger up-close, a quick look inside his enormous mouth doesn’t come without a risk!

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Former police officer Ahron is tracking a stolen white MG taken during a spate of car thefts in Leeds. He discovers an illegal chop shop where vehicles are being broken up for parts. There’s a stolen vehicle there, waiting to be dismantled, but there’s no sign of the white MG. Is Ahron too late? A family preparing to celebrate Diwali has their Lexus taken from outside their home in South Woodford, London. A month later, stolen vehicle examiner Adam and his team find it in a shipping container at Felixstowe port. If it hadn’t been spotted, the stolen vehicle would have been shipped overseas, never to be seen again. In Dartford, Kent, tracker Jason snatches back a car belonging to a rental company after the driver refuses to hand it back. Making things even worse, he’s been clocked speeding no fewer than three times!

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: Rachel Nickell was murdered in 1992. Ten years later, a team using new DNA technology finally identify her killer. In another case, a trace expert uses beer glass fragments to find an assailant.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Caroline Hawley soaks up the fascinating story of Malvern’s popularity as a spa town. Visitors flocked to the Worcestershire town in the Victorian era to cure all manner of ailments, bathing in and drinking the spring water gushing out of the Malvern Hills. Notable patients included Florence Nightingale, Charles Darwin and Charles Dickens's wife, Catherine. Hoping for a healthy profit at auction are two teams of students hunting for bargains with their experts David Fergus and Thomas Forrester. Aiming to school the blues are student teachers Sophie and Bethany, and hoping to make their mark on the map are their opponents, geography undergraduates Patrick and Freya. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds make an unseasonal stop at a stall selling an American steerable sledge, but with an asking price of three figures, the team veer away from it. Meanwhile, the blues wonder if an airline cargo sign might meet their expert's challenge, but Thomas doesn’t think it’s a flyer! The teams touch down in Bristol, where auctioneer Andy Stowe reveals his estimates on their items before he taxis to the rostrum to sell them in front of a roomful of bidders.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: The Hairdresser Mysteries
programme.desc: As the village prepares for a celebratory concert at the theatre, Lily and Clary realise the sudden death of one of the acts is not what it seems. Singer Heather Small guest-stars.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Feeling an affinity for Wales, and in particular the island of Anglesey, a Canadian couple task Briony May Williams with finding them the stone cottage they’ve always dreamed of owning for their budget of £450,000. Briony also visits the island’s sea zoo to learn about their work conserving endangered marine life, including the sedentary seahorse.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Former miner Peter Lawson is the beating heart of Durham’s Easington Colliery Band. He joined the band at 11 and has worked tirelessly for 55 years to keep it going. From managing the band, to moving equipment and raising money with a band cafe, the list is endless. His dedication has seen the band grow and in 2024 win the North of England Championships. Last year, they also performed with music legend Sam Fender. Seventy-five years ago, the mining community suffered one of the north east’s worst pit disasters. The band united the community and played at every one of funerals of the 83 men that died. To mark the anniversary, the band is preparing for their biggest concert at Durham Cathedral. Teacher Dan is busy recruiting new band members to play, and local children are rehearsing their contribution, A Miner’s Song, so that it can be ready for the concert. But with Peter unwell with what could be a serious condition, and Dan and Georgia expecting a baby the week of the concert, will the key members of the band be there? And if Peter retires, what happens to the band? Will the next generation step up to the challenge?

programme.title: Granite Harbour
programme.desc: Lindo and the team recover the murder weapon and find new leads that challenge their assumptions as tensions rise within the community.

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon hosts the award-winning comedy panel show, with Lee Mack and David Mitchell as the lightning-quick team captains. Each week, a stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal extraordinary stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? Sorting the fact from the fiction are guest panellists Kadeena Cox, Ivo Graham, Harriet Kemsley and Eddie Marsan.

programme.title: Ann Droid
programme.desc: Linda encourages Sue to join Tom and Eileen on a trip to the seaside to scatter ashes. To cheer themselves up, they decide to go to a funfair, where a fortune teller leaves Sue hoping for a sign from Dave and a promise to try new things, starting with a rollercoaster ride. Meanwhile, Michael’s efforts to be a rock star and impress everyone at an open-mic night are totally ruined thanks to Linda.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: There’s growing concern for Malaika, the elderly lioness, whose health has been deteriorating. The keepers and vets decide that their only option is to sedate her to find out what’s been troubling her, but knocking out any animal, especially an elderly one, is a risk. At nearly 20 years old, she now faces a fresh diagnosis, but will they be able to get this wily old girl to take the medication that could help her? Meanwhile, there’s cause for celebration in Animal Adventure, where red squirrel parents Rory and Pinecone have had a litter of elusive new kittens – Megan checks in with keeper Chris to find out how they’re getting on. Also, Kate and Ben join forces to help carry out vital health checks on Red, the largest Amur tiger at the park. It’s essential keepers continually assess his fitness and health, but when you’re dealing with a tiger up-close, a quick look inside his enormous mouth doesn’t come without a risk!

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Former police officer Ahron is tracking a stolen white MG taken during a spate of car thefts in Leeds. He discovers an illegal chop shop where vehicles are being broken up for parts. There’s a stolen vehicle there, waiting to be dismantled, but there’s no sign of the white MG. Is Ahron too late? A family preparing to celebrate Diwali has their Lexus taken from outside their home in South Woodford, London. A month later, stolen vehicle examiner Adam and his team find it in a shipping container at Felixstowe port. If it hadn’t been spotted, the stolen vehicle would have been shipped overseas, never to be seen again. In Dartford, Kent, tracker Jason snatches back a car belonging to a rental company after the driver refuses to hand it back. Making things even worse, he’s been clocked speeding no fewer than three times!

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Caroline Hawley soaks up the fascinating story of Malvern’s popularity as a spa town. Visitors flocked to the Worcestershire town in the Victorian era to cure all manner of ailments, bathing in and drinking the spring water gushing out of the Malvern Hills. Notable patients included Florence Nightingale, Charles Darwin and Charles Dickens's wife, Catherine. Hoping for a healthy profit at auction are two teams of students hunting for bargains with their experts David Fergus and Thomas Forrester. Aiming to school the blues are student teachers Sophie and Bethany, and hoping to make their mark on the map are their opponents, geography undergraduates Patrick and Freya. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds make an unseasonal stop at a stall selling an American steerable sledge, but with an asking price of three figures, the team veer away from it. Meanwhile, the blues wonder if an airline cargo sign might meet their expert's challenge, but Thomas doesn’t think it’s a flyer! The teams touch down in Bristol, where auctioneer Andy Stowe reveals his estimates on their items before he taxis to the rostrum to sell them in front of a roomful of bidders.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Caroline Hawley soaks up the fascinating story of Malvern’s popularity as a spa town. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds make an unseasonal stop at a stall selling an American steerable sledge, but with an asking price of three figures, the team veer away from it. The teams touch down in Bristol, where auctioneer Andy Stowe reveals his estimates on their items before he taxis to the rostrum to sell them in front of a roomful of bidders.

Visitors flocked to the Worcestershire town in the Victorian era to cure all manner of ailments, bathing in and drinking the spring water gushing out of the Malvern Hills. Notable patients included Florence Nightingale, Charles Darwin and Charles Dickens's wife, Catherine. Hoping for a healthy profit at auction are two teams of students hunting for bargains with their experts David Fergus and Thomas Forrester. Aiming to school the blues are student teachers Sophie and Bethany, and hoping to make their mark on the map are their opponents, geography undergraduates Patrick and Freya. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds make an unseasonal stop at a stall selling an American steerable sledge, but with an asking price of three figures, the team veer away from it. Meanwhile, the blues wonder if an airline cargo sign might meet their expert's challenge, but Thomas doesn’t think it’s a flyer! The teams touch down in Bristol, where auctioneer Andy Stowe reveals his estimates on their items before he taxis to the rostrum to sell them in front of a roomful of bidders.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: The Hairdresser Mysteries
programme.desc: As the village prepares for a celebratory concert at the theatre, Lily and Clary realise the sudden death of one of the acts is not what it seems. Singer Heather Small guest-stars.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Feeling an affinity for Wales, and in particular the island of Anglesey, a Canadian couple task Briony May Williams with finding them the stone cottage they’ve always dreamed of owning for their budget of £450,000. Briony also visits the island’s sea zoo to learn about their work conserving endangered marine life, including the sedentary seahorse.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: After losing both parents, siblings Sarah and James call in JB and Saf to help turn heirlooms into a dream holiday. Will Mouseman creations and cricket books bowl over the bidders?

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns - but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Stephen Mangan. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: BBC News at Six
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.desc: The latest news, sport and weather for the North East and Cumbria.

programme.title: The One Show
programme.desc: Vernon Kay and JB Gill bring you the stories that matter from across the country.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Former miner Peter Lawson is the beating heart of Durham’s Easington Colliery Band. He joined the band at 11 and has worked tirelessly for 55 years to keep it going. From managing the band, to moving equipment and raising money with a band cafe, the list is endless. His dedication has seen the band grow and in 2024 win the North of England Championships. Last year, they also performed with music legend Sam Fender. Seventy-five years ago, the mining community suffered one of the north east’s worst pit disasters. The band united the community and played at every one of funerals of the 83 men that died. To mark the anniversary, the band is preparing for their biggest concert at Durham Cathedral. Teacher Dan is busy recruiting new band members to play, and local children are rehearsing their contribution, A Miner’s Song, so that it can be ready for the concert. But with Peter unwell with what could be a serious condition, and Dan and Georgia expecting a baby the week of the concert, will the key members of the band be there? And if Peter retires, what happens to the band? Will the next generation step up to the challenge?

programme.title: Granite Harbour
programme.desc: Lindo and the team recover the murder weapon and find new leads that challenge their assumptions as tensions rise within the community.

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon hosts the award-winning comedy panel show, with Lee Mack and David Mitchell as the lightning-quick team captains. Each week, a stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal extraordinary stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? Sorting the fact from the fiction are guest panellists Kadeena Cox, Ivo Graham, Harriet Kemsley and Eddie Marsan.

programme.title: Ann Droid
programme.desc: Linda encourages Sue to join Tom and Eileen on a trip to the seaside to scatter ashes. To cheer themselves up, they decide to go to a funfair, where a fortune teller leaves Sue hoping for a sign from Dave and a promise to try new things, starting with a rollercoaster ride. Meanwhile, Michael’s efforts to be a rock star and impress everyone at an open-mic night are totally ruined thanks to Linda.

programme.title: BBC News at Ten
programme.desc: The latest national and international news, with reports from BBC correspondents worldwide.

programme.title: Look North (North East and Cumbria)
programme.desc: The latest news, sport and weather for the North East and Cumbria.

programme.title: Austin
programme.desc: Austin follows a romcom manual to woo Haley, Ingrid flirts with Big Bear, and a kiss leads to disaster when the bear's head comes off – literally.

programme.title: Austin
programme.desc: Ingrid quits Big Bear, Austin cancels fame, Mel races to stop a resignation, and Haley might be 'The One'. All roads lead to Thunder Thursday and one gloriously chaotic Canberra bus ride.

programme.title: Scent of a Woman
programme.desc: Lt Col Frank Slad is a bombastic retired army officer who has lost his sight but has not lost his passion for living. Charlie Simms is a young college student who takes a job watching over the blind iconoclast. He learns rather quickly, however, how much he has yet to see and how much life he has yet to experience.

programme.title: Alan Carr's Picture Slam
programme.desc: Comedian Alan Carr hosts the fun and frantic quiz show where every question is a picture and every picture is worth cash. They could be anything from famous faces, places, products or logos, and teams need to name them all for a Picture Slam. Playing this time are friends Olivia and Danny from Bury St Edmunds, siblings Will and Charmain from Combe Martin, plus mum and daughter Sharon and Lucy from Staffordshire. They battle it out across four rounds, shouting out answers and building their banks. But only one team can make it to the final Super Slam for the chance to win £10,000.

programme.title: Joins BBC News
programme.desc: BBC One joins the BBC's rolling news channel for a night of news.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: There’s growing concern for Malaika, the elderly lioness, whose health has been deteriorating. The keepers and vets decide that their only option is to sedate her to find out what’s been troubling her, but knocking out any animal, especially an elderly one, is a risk. At nearly 20 years old, she now faces a fresh diagnosis, but will they be able to get this wily old girl to take the medication that could help her? Meanwhile, there’s cause for celebration in Animal Adventure, where red squirrel parents Rory and Pinecone have had a litter of elusive new kittens – Megan checks in with keeper Chris to find out how they’re getting on. Also, Kate and Ben join forces to help carry out vital health checks on Red, the largest Amur tiger at the park. It’s essential keepers continually assess his fitness and health, but when you’re dealing with a tiger up-close, a quick look inside his enormous mouth doesn’t come without a risk!

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Former police officer Ahron is tracking a stolen white MG taken during a spate of car thefts in Leeds. He discovers an illegal chop shop where vehicles are being broken up for parts. There’s a stolen vehicle there, waiting to be dismantled, but there’s no sign of the white MG. Is Ahron too late? A family preparing to celebrate Diwali has their Lexus taken from outside their home in South Woodford, London. A month later, stolen vehicle examiner Adam and his team find it in a shipping container at Felixstowe port. If it hadn’t been spotted, the stolen vehicle would have been shipped overseas, never to be seen again. In Dartford, Kent, tracker Jason snatches back a car belonging to a rental company after the driver refuses to hand it back. Making things even worse, he’s been clocked speeding no fewer than three times!

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: Rachel Nickell was murdered in 1992. Ten years later, a team using new DNA technology finally identify her killer. In another case, a trace expert uses beer glass fragments to find an assailant.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: There’s growing concern for Malaika, the elderly lioness, whose health has been deteriorating. The keepers and vets decide that their only option is to sedate her to find out what’s been troubling her, but knocking out any animal, especially an elderly one, is a risk. At nearly 20 years old, she now faces a fresh diagnosis, but will they be able to get this wily old girl to take the medication that could help her? Meanwhile, there’s cause for celebration in Animal Adventure, where red squirrel parents Rory and Pinecone have had a litter of elusive new kittens – Megan checks in with keeper Chris to find out how they’re getting on. Also, Kate and Ben join forces to help carry out vital health checks on Red, the largest Amur tiger at the park. It’s essential keepers continually assess his fitness and health, but when you’re dealing with a tiger up-close, a quick look inside his enormous mouth doesn’t come without a risk!

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Former police officer Ahron is tracking a stolen white MG taken during a spate of car thefts in Leeds. He discovers an illegal chop shop where vehicles are being broken up for parts. There’s a stolen vehicle there, waiting to be dismantled, but there’s no sign of the white MG. Is Ahron too late? A family preparing to celebrate Diwali has their Lexus taken from outside their home in South Woodford, London. A month later, stolen vehicle examiner Adam and his team find it in a shipping container at Felixstowe port. If it hadn’t been spotted, the stolen vehicle would have been shipped overseas, never to be seen again. In Dartford, Kent, tracker Jason snatches back a car belonging to a rental company after the driver refuses to hand it back. Making things even worse, he’s been clocked speeding no fewer than three times!

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: Rachel Nickell was murdered in 1992. Ten years later, a team using new DNA technology finally identify her killer. In another case, a trace expert uses beer glass fragments to find an assailant.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Caroline Hawley soaks up the fascinating story of Malvern’s popularity as a spa town. Visitors flocked to the Worcestershire town in the Victorian era to cure all manner of ailments, bathing in and drinking the spring water gushing out of the Malvern Hills. Notable patients included Florence Nightingale, Charles Darwin and Charles Dickens's wife, Catherine. Hoping for a healthy profit at auction are two teams of students hunting for bargains with their experts David Fergus and Thomas Forrester. Aiming to school the blues are student teachers Sophie and Bethany, and hoping to make their mark on the map are their opponents, geography undergraduates Patrick and Freya. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds make an unseasonal stop at a stall selling an American steerable sledge, but with an asking price of three figures, the team veer away from it. Meanwhile, the blues wonder if an airline cargo sign might meet their expert's challenge, but Thomas doesn’t think it’s a flyer! The teams touch down in Bristol, where auctioneer Andy Stowe reveals his estimates on their items before he taxis to the rostrum to sell them in front of a roomful of bidders.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Feeling an affinity for Wales, and in particular the island of Anglesey, a Canadian couple task Briony May Williams with finding them the stone cottage they’ve always dreamed of owning for their budget of £450,000. Briony also visits the island’s sea zoo to learn about their work conserving endangered marine life, including the sedentary seahorse.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Our Lives

The band united the community and played at every one of funerals of the 83 men that died. To mark the anniversary, the band is preparing for their biggest concert at Durham Cathedral. Teacher Dan is busy recruiting new band members to play, and local children are rehearsing their contribution, A Miner’s Song, so that it can be ready for the concert. But with Peter unwell with what could be a serious condition, and Dan and Georgia expecting a baby the week of the concert, will the key members of the band be there? And if Peter retires, what happens to the band? Will the next generation step up to the challenge?

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: There’s growing concern for Malaika, the elderly lioness, whose health has been deteriorating. The keepers and vets decide that their only option is to sedate her to find out what’s been troubling her, but knocking out any animal, especially an elderly one, is a risk. At nearly 20 years old, she now faces a fresh diagnosis, but will they be able to get this wily old girl to take the medication that could help her? Meanwhile, there’s cause for celebration in Animal Adventure, where red squirrel parents Rory and Pinecone have had a litter of elusive new kittens – Megan checks in with keeper Chris to find out how they’re getting on. Also, Kate and Ben join forces to help carry out vital health checks on Red, the largest Amur tiger at the park. It’s essential keepers continually assess his fitness and health, but when you’re dealing with a tiger up-close, a quick look inside his enormous mouth doesn’t come without a risk!

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Former police officer Ahron is tracking a stolen white MG taken during a spate of car thefts in Leeds. He discovers an illegal chop shop where vehicles are being broken up for parts. There’s a stolen vehicle there, waiting to be dismantled, but there’s no sign of the white MG. Is Ahron too late? A family preparing to celebrate Diwali has their Lexus taken from outside their home in South Woodford, London. A month later, stolen vehicle examiner Adam and his team find it in a shipping container at Felixstowe port. If it hadn’t been spotted, the stolen vehicle would have been shipped overseas, never to be seen again. In Dartford, Kent, tracker Jason snatches back a car belonging to a rental company after the driver refuses to hand it back. Making things even worse, he’s been clocked speeding no fewer than three times!

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: Rachel Nickell was murdered in 1992. Ten years later, a team using new DNA technology finally identify her killer. In another case, a trace expert uses beer glass fragments to find an assailant.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Caroline Hawley soaks up the fascinating story of Malvern’s popularity as a spa town. Visitors flocked to the Worcestershire town in the Victorian era to cure all manner of ailments, bathing in and drinking the spring water gushing out of the Malvern Hills. Notable patients included Florence Nightingale, Charles Darwin and Charles Dickens's wife, Catherine. Hoping for a healthy profit at auction are two teams of students hunting for bargains with their experts David Fergus and Thomas Forrester. Aiming to school the blues are student teachers Sophie and Bethany, and hoping to make their mark on the map are their opponents, geography undergraduates Patrick and Freya. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds make an unseasonal stop at a stall selling an American steerable sledge, but with an asking price of three figures, the team veer away from it. Meanwhile, the blues wonder if an airline cargo sign might meet their expert's challenge, but Thomas doesn’t think it’s a flyer! The teams touch down in Bristol, where auctioneer Andy Stowe reveals his estimates on their items before he taxis to the rostrum to sell them in front of a roomful of bidders.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Feeling an affinity for Wales, and in particular the island of Anglesey, a Canadian couple task Briony May Williams with finding them the stone cottage they’ve always dreamed of owning for their budget of £450,000. Briony also visits the island’s sea zoo to learn about their work conserving endangered marine life, including the sedentary seahorse.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.desc: Former miner Peter Lawson is the beating heart of Durham’s Easington Colliery Band. He joined the band at 11 and has worked tirelessly for 55 years to keep it going. From managing the band, to moving equipment and raising money with a band cafe, the list is endless. His dedication has seen the band grow and in 2024 win the North of England Championships. Last year, they also performed with music legend Sam Fender. Seventy-five years ago, the mining community suffered one of the north east’s worst pit disasters. The band united the community and played at every one of funerals of the 83 men that died. To mark the anniversary, the band is preparing for their biggest concert at Durham Cathedral. Teacher Dan is busy recruiting new band members to play, and local children are rehearsing their contribution, A Miner’s Song, so that it can be ready for the concert. But with Peter unwell with what could be a serious condition, and Dan and Georgia expecting a baby the week of the concert, will the key members of the band be there? And if Peter retires, what happens to the band? Will the next generation step up to the challenge?

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: There’s growing concern for Malaika, the elderly lioness, whose health has been deteriorating. The keepers and vets decide that their only option is to sedate her to find out what’s been troubling her, but knocking out any animal, especially an elderly one, is a risk. At nearly 20 years old, she now faces a fresh diagnosis, but will they be able to get this wily old girl to take the medication that could help her? Meanwhile, there’s cause for celebration in Animal Adventure, where red squirrel parents Rory and Pinecone have had a litter of elusive new kittens – Megan checks in with keeper Chris to find out how they’re getting on. Also, Kate and Ben join forces to help carry out vital health checks on Red, the largest Amur tiger at the park. It’s essential keepers continually assess his fitness and health, but when you’re dealing with a tiger up-close, a quick look inside his enormous mouth doesn’t come without a risk!

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Former police officer Ahron is tracking a stolen white MG taken during a spate of car thefts in Leeds. He discovers an illegal chop shop where vehicles are being broken up for parts. There’s a stolen vehicle there, waiting to be dismantled, but there’s no sign of the white MG. Is Ahron too late? A family preparing to celebrate Diwali has their Lexus taken from outside their home in South Woodford, London. A month later, stolen vehicle examiner Adam and his team find it in a shipping container at Felixstowe port. If it hadn’t been spotted, the stolen vehicle would have been shipped overseas, never to be seen again. In Dartford, Kent, tracker Jason snatches back a car belonging to a rental company after the driver refuses to hand it back. Making things even worse, he’s been clocked speeding no fewer than three times!

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: Rachel Nickell was murdered in 1992. Ten years later, a team using new DNA technology finally identify her killer. In another case, a trace expert uses beer glass fragments to find an assailant.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Caroline Hawley soaks up the fascinating story of Malvern’s popularity as a spa town. Visitors flocked to the Worcestershire town in the Victorian era to cure all manner of ailments, bathing in and drinking the spring water gushing out of the Malvern Hills. Notable patients included Florence Nightingale, Charles Darwin and Charles Dickens's wife, Catherine. Hoping for a healthy profit at auction are two teams of students hunting for bargains with their experts David Fergus and Thomas Forrester. Aiming to school the blues are student teachers Sophie and Bethany, and hoping to make their mark on the map are their opponents, geography undergraduates Patrick and Freya. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds make an unseasonal stop at a stall selling an American steerable sledge, but with an asking price of three figures, the team veer away from it. Meanwhile, the blues wonder if an airline cargo sign might meet their expert's challenge, but Thomas doesn’t think it’s a flyer! The teams touch down in Bristol, where auctioneer Andy Stowe reveals his estimates on their items before he taxis to the rostrum to sell them in front of a roomful of bidders.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

Visitors flocked to the Worcestershire town in the Victorian era to cure all manner of ailments, bathing in and drinking the spring water gushing out of the Malvern Hills. Notable patients included Florence Nightingale, Charles Darwin and Charles Dickens's wife, Catherine. Hoping for a healthy profit at auction are two teams of students hunting for bargains with their experts David Fergus and Thomas Forrester. Aiming to school the blues are student teachers Sophie and Bethany, and hoping to make their mark on the map are their opponents, geography undergraduates Patrick and Freya. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds make an unseasonal stop at a stall selling an American steerable sledge, but with an asking price of three figures, the team veer away from it. Meanwhile, the blues wonder if an airline cargo sign might meet their expert's challenge, but Thomas doesn’t think it’s a flyer! The teams touch down in Bristol, where auctioneer Andy Stowe reveals his estimates on their items before he taxis to the rostrum to sell them in front of a roomful of bidders.

programme.title: The Bidding Room

Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: There’s growing concern for Malaika, the elderly lioness, whose health has been deteriorating. The keepers and vets decide that their only option is to sedate her to find out what’s been troubling her, but knocking out any animal, especially an elderly one, is a risk. At nearly 20 years old, she now faces a fresh diagnosis, but will they be able to get this wily old girl to take the medication that could help her? Meanwhile, there’s cause for celebration in Animal Adventure, where red squirrel parents Rory and Pinecone have had a litter of elusive new kittens – Megan checks in with keeper Chris to find out how they’re getting on. Also, Kate and Ben join forces to help carry out vital health checks on Red, the largest Amur tiger at the park. It’s essential keepers continually assess his fitness and health, but when you’re dealing with a tiger up-close, a quick look inside his enormous mouth doesn’t come without a risk!

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Former police officer Ahron is tracking a stolen white MG taken during a spate of car thefts in Leeds. He discovers an illegal chop shop where vehicles are being broken up for parts. There’s a stolen vehicle there, waiting to be dismantled, but there’s no sign of the white MG. Is Ahron too late? A family preparing to celebrate Diwali has their Lexus taken from outside their home in South Woodford, London. A month later, stolen vehicle examiner Adam and his team find it in a shipping container at Felixstowe port. If it hadn’t been spotted, the stolen vehicle would have been shipped overseas, never to be seen again. In Dartford, Kent, tracker Jason snatches back a car belonging to a rental company after the driver refuses to hand it back. Making things even worse, he’s been clocked speeding no fewer than three times!

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Former miner Peter Lawson is the beating heart of Durham’s Easington Colliery Band. He joined the band at 11 and has worked tirelessly for 55 years to keep it going. From managing the band, to moving equipment and raising money with a band cafe, the list is endless. His dedication has seen the band grow and in 2024 win the North of England Championships. Last year, they also performed with music legend Sam Fender. Seventy-five years ago, the mining community suffered one of the north east’s worst pit disasters. The band united the community and played at every one of funerals of the 83 men that died. To mark the anniversary, the band is preparing for their biggest concert at Durham Cathedral. Teacher Dan is busy recruiting new band members to play, and local children are rehearsing their contribution, A Miner’s Song, so that it can be ready for the concert. But with Peter unwell with what could be a serious condition, and Dan and Georgia expecting a baby the week of the concert, will the key members of the band be there? And if Peter retires, what happens to the band? Will the next generation step up to the challenge?

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: There’s growing concern for Malaika, the elderly lioness, whose health has been deteriorating. The keepers and vets decide that their only option is to sedate her to find out what’s been troubling her, but knocking out any animal, especially an elderly one, is a risk. At nearly 20 years old, she now faces a fresh diagnosis, but will they be able to get this wily old girl to take the medication that could help her? Meanwhile, there’s cause for celebration in Animal Adventure, where red squirrel parents Rory and Pinecone have had a litter of elusive new kittens – Megan checks in with keeper Chris to find out how they’re getting on. Also, Kate and Ben join forces to help carry out vital health checks on Red, the largest Amur tiger at the park. It’s essential keepers continually assess his fitness and health, but when you’re dealing with a tiger up-close, a quick look inside his enormous mouth doesn’t come without a risk!

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Former police officer Ahron is tracking a stolen white MG taken during a spate of car thefts in Leeds. He discovers an illegal chop shop where vehicles are being broken up for parts. There’s a stolen vehicle there, waiting to be dismantled, but there’s no sign of the white MG. Is Ahron too late? A family preparing to celebrate Diwali has their Lexus taken from outside their home in South Woodford, London. A month later, stolen vehicle examiner Adam and his team find it in a shipping container at Felixstowe port. If it hadn’t been spotted, the stolen vehicle would have been shipped overseas, never to be seen again. In Dartford, Kent, tracker Jason snatches back a car belonging to a rental company after the driver refuses to hand it back. Making things even worse, he’s been clocked speeding no fewer than three times!

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: Rachel Nickell was murdered in 1992. Ten years later, a team using new DNA technology finally identify her killer. In another case, a trace expert uses beer glass fragments to find an assailant.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Caroline Hawley soaks up the fascinating story of Malvern’s popularity as a spa town. Visitors flocked to the Worcestershire town in the Victorian era to cure all manner of ailments, bathing in and drinking the spring water gushing out of the Malvern Hills. Notable patients included Florence Nightingale, Charles Darwin and Charles Dickens's wife, Catherine. Hoping for a healthy profit at auction are two teams of students hunting for bargains with their experts David Fergus and Thomas Forrester. Aiming to school the blues are student teachers Sophie and Bethany, and hoping to make their mark on the map are their opponents, geography undergraduates Patrick and Freya. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds make an unseasonal stop at a stall selling an American steerable sledge, but with an asking price of three figures, the team veer away from it. Meanwhile, the blues wonder if an airline cargo sign might meet their expert's challenge, but Thomas doesn’t think it’s a flyer! The teams touch down in Bristol, where auctioneer Andy Stowe reveals his estimates on their items before he taxis to the rostrum to sell them in front of a roomful of bidders.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Feeling an affinity for Wales, and in particular the island of Anglesey, a Canadian couple task Briony May Williams with finding them the stone cottage they’ve always dreamed of owning for their budget of £450,000. Briony also visits the island’s sea zoo to learn about their work conserving endangered marine life, including the sedentary seahorse.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Former miner Peter Lawson is the beating heart of Durham’s Easington Colliery Band. He joined the band at 11 and has worked tirelessly for 55 years to keep it going. From managing the band, to moving equipment and raising money with a band cafe, the list is endless. His dedication has seen the band grow and in 2024 win the North of England Championships. Last year, they also performed with music legend Sam Fender. Seventy-five years ago, the mining community suffered one of the north east’s worst pit disasters. The band united the community and played at every one of funerals of the 83 men that died. To mark the anniversary, the band is preparing for their biggest concert at Durham Cathedral. Teacher Dan is busy recruiting new band members to play, and local children are rehearsing their contribution, A Miner’s Song, so that it can be ready for the concert. But with Peter unwell with what could be a serious condition, and Dan and Georgia expecting a baby the week of the concert, will the key members of the band be there? And if Peter retires, what happens to the band? Will the next generation step up to the challenge?

programme.title: Granite Harbour
programme.desc: Lindo and the team recover the murder weapon and find new leads that challenge their assumptions as tensions rise within the community.

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon hosts the award-winning comedy panel show, with Lee Mack and David Mitchell as the lightning-quick team captains. Each week, a stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal extraordinary stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? Sorting the fact from the fiction are guest panellists Kadeena Cox, Ivo Graham, Harriet Kemsley and Eddie Marsan.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Former miner Peter Lawson is the beating heart of Durham’s Easington Colliery Band. He joined the band at 11 and has worked tirelessly for 55 years to keep it going. From managing the band, to moving equipment and raising money with a band cafe, the list is endless. His dedication has seen the band grow and in 2024 win the North of England Championships. programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: There’s growing concern for Malaika, the elderly lioness, whose health has been deteriorating. The keepers and vets decide that their only option is to sedate her to find out what’s been troubling her, but knocking out any animal, especially an elderly one, is a risk. At nearly 20 years old, she now faces a fresh diagnosis, but will they be able to get this wily old girl to take the medication that could help her? Meanwhile, there’s cause for celebration in Animal Adventure, where red squirrel parents Rory and Pinecone have had a litter of elusive new kittens – Megan checks in with keeper Chris to find out how they’re getting on. Also, Kate and Ben join forces to help carry out vital health checks on Red, the largest Amur tiger at the park. It’s essential keepers continually assess his fitness and health, but when you’re dealing with a tiger up-close, a quick look inside his enormous mouth doesn’t come without a risk!

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Former police officer Ahron is tracking a stolen white MG taken during a spate of car thefts in Leeds. He discovers an illegal chop shop where vehicles are being broken up for parts. There’s a stolen vehicle there, waiting to be dismantled, but there’s no sign of the white MG. Is Ahron too late? A family preparing to celebrate Diwali has their Lexus taken from outside their home in South Woodford, London. A month later, stolen vehicle examiner Adam and his team find it in a shipping container at Felixstowe port. If it hadn’t been spotted, the stolen vehicle would have been shipped overseas, never to be seen again. In Dartford, Kent, tracker Jason snatches back a car belonging to a rental company after the driver refuses to hand it back. Making things even worse, he’s been clocked speeding no fewer than three times!

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: Rachel Nickell was murdered in 1992. Ten years later, a team using new DNA technology finally identify her killer. In another case, a trace expert uses beer glass fragments to find an assailant.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Caroline Hawley soaks up the fascinating story of Malvern’s popularity as a spa town. Visitors flocked to the Worcestershire town in the Victorian era to cure all manner of ailments, bathing in and drinking the spring water gushing out of the Malvern Hills. Notable patients included Florence Nightingale, Charles Darwin and Charles Dickens's wife, Catherine. Hoping for a healthy profit at auction are two teams of students hunting for bargains with their experts David Fergus and Thomas Forrester. Aiming to school the blues are student teachers Sophie and Bethany, and hoping to make their mark on the map are their opponents, geography undergraduates Patrick and Freya. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds make an unseasonal stop at a stall selling an American steerable sledge, but with an asking price of three figures, the team veer away from it. Meanwhile, the blues wonder if an airline cargo sign might meet their expert's challenge, but Thomas doesn’t think it’s a flyer! The teams touch down in Bristol, where auctioneer Andy Stowe reveals his estimates on their items before he taxis to the rostrum to sell them in front of a roomful of bidders.

programme.desc: More from the day’s top stories and communities across Scotland.

programme.title: Scotland's Greatest Escape
programme.desc: Scotland's Greatest Historic Escape is chosen by Mathew, his girlfriend Alexandra, little brother Malachi and mum Amanda, from Fife. This family of jetsetters have travelled all over the world but have never had a holiday in Scotland. They're stepping back in time to decide whether Douneside House, an Aberdeenshire retreat with a military past, 500-year-old Kilmartin Castle in Argyll and Bute, or The Lovat, a former train station hotel on the shores of Loch Ness, is their favourite.

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: In Glasgow, Paul and Ryan of the Special Operations Response Team are called to a siege in a flat where a man has barricaded himself inside and is threatening to harm himself. It’s a difficult and emotional situation, and the team must coordinate with the police at the scene to try to ensure the best outcome. Meanwhile, Aberdeen-based teammates Kirsty and Bruce are called to see Rebecca, who has suffered an anaphylactic attack. The crew administer several doses of adrenaline, but Rebecca shows little signs of improvement, prompting a rapid journey on blue lights to Aberdeen Royal Infirmary. From the lowlands to the Highlands, the Scottish Air Ambulance Service delivers help to every part of the country. Serving as a paramedic on the King Air fixed-wing aircraft, Stephen travels to the Isle of Lewis. William is visiting the islands as part of a golfing holiday but has fractured his ribs in a fall, necessitating a transfer to the mainland.

programme.title: Rikki
programme.desc: A centenary celebration of the life and legacy of Rikki Fulton, one of Scotland’s most beloved comic actors. Ashley Jensen narrates an affectionate tribute to one of Scotland’s funniest comedians, Rikki Fulton. It’s 100 years since Rikki first made an entrance on to the world stage and 20 years since he bowed out. For decades, he’s been making the nation laugh with his rubber face, razor sharp wit and laconic demeanour. His influence is still felt in new generations of comics, and clips of his sketches still make us laugh to this day. This programme tells the story of his extraordinary life by bringing together the people closest to him and the people he inspired. It delves deep into the vaults with the help of some never-before-seen home movie footage to discover the story of the real man behind the genius and showcase the best-loved moments of his career - from his iconic long-running characters such as Francie and Josie, IM Jolly and Supercop to the one-off sketches such as Terrible Burns and The Driving Instructor. We’ll also feature his memorable appearances in movies such as Local Hero and Gorky Park.

programme.title: Still Game
programme.desc: Sitcom featuring Jack and Victor, two irrepressible pensioners first seen in the comedy series Chewin' the Fat, along with their dependable pals Winston and Tam, fresh out of Craiglang and taking on the world. Yankee happy pills are proving more of a temptation to Jack and Victor after they bump into their old pal Stuart.

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: Party-seeking Cathy and her henpecked husband Colin are back from an Italian holiday and excited to be hosting a soiree at their house - arranged for the purpose of showing off how popular they are. They’ve invited Gail and Andy, the fabulous Amalfi friends they met in Sorrento – but as the duty-free wine flows and the guests of honour begin to bond a bit too much with the neighbours, Cathy and Colin’s tensions soon bubble to the surface. With Colin unashamedly competing with Andy to be the alpha male in the room, and Cathy desperately trying to cling on to the good times with Gail, their much-anticipated party is left in tatters.

programme.title: Rip It Up
programme.desc: Series about the success story of Scottish pop. This episode traces the humble beginnings of some of Scotland's biggest-ever bands and shows how they evolved.

programme.desc: The Australian version of the hit UK series. When city couple Kate and Sean inherit Ramshead Manor, a run-down country estate, they see it as a sign for a fresh new start. But after Kate has a near-death experience, she gains the ability to see and hear ghosts – and discovers there are several living in the mansion. Kate must navigate the ghosts' issues while trying to start a hotel business with Sean, who remains unable to see them.

programme.title: Fleabag
programme.desc: The eponymous Fleabag returns, joining an uncomfortable family dinner to celebrate Godmother and Dad’s engagement. Alongside familiar faces - uptight sister Claire and her alcoholic husband Martin - Fleabag find herself intrigued by Godmother’s new priest. The evening comes to a tempestuous end, however, when an unexpected attack brings old tensions bubbling to the surface.

programme.title: Fleabag
programme.desc: A counselling session elicits an uncomfortable truth from Fleabag, and she finds herself somewhere unexpected. Elsewhere, a chat with Claire brings some unwelcome news, Martin and Fleabag face off, and Jake wonders where Claire is.

programme.title: Fleabag
programme.desc: BBC Three presents... Fleabag helps with an event at Claire's work which inevitably ends in disaster, but an introduction to Claire's colleague proves intriguing, and a chance meeting with a stranger opens Fleabag's eyes.

programme.title: Ambulance
programme.desc: Critical care paramedic Matt administers pain relief to patient Neil before he is rushed to hospital, where doctors will assess him for suspected head and neck injuries.

programme.title: Evolution
programme.desc: How did the ostrich come to lay the biggest egg on earth? Chris Packham explores the way reproduction has shaped life on earth and the surprising evolutionary origins of sex, eggs and birds. It's a four-billion-year journey contained within a shell.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. programme.title: Marcus Wareing Simply Provence
programme.desc: Marcus is visiting a local farmers' market, where each week a local French chef impresses the crowds with a live cooking demo. However, he’s been told a British chef is cooking tonight, and that chef… is Marcus. Can he convince the locals that Brits know how to cook? Later, Marcus has a VIP guest coming for dinner, the mayor of St Remy’s sister, and he really wants to impress. As she is a bit of a history buff, he decides to do some research into the origins of some local produce to find culinary inspiration.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Lifeline
programme.desc: Eddie Marsan presents this month’s Lifeline appeal on behalf of Tourettes Action, a charity which provides support, information and advocacy to improve the lives of people living with Tourette syndrome and their families.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week the celebrity contestants Yasmine Akram, Cariad Lloyd, Geoff Norcott and Dennis Taylor take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quick-fire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games kitchen composter?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple - make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Hairy Bikers' Bakeation
programme.desc: The home of Mozart, The Sound of Music and Arnold Schwarzenegger provides the fifth leg of the Hairy Bikers' adventure. The trip starts in Vienna, patisserie capital of the world, and ends atop the spectacular Grossglockner Alpine pass, one of the world's most spectacular biking roads. In Vienna, Si and Dave unravel the mystery of the two competing sachertorte recipes and taste the latest version - sachertorte 'reloaded'. They make apfelstrudel with the owner of a roadside B&B, cook linzertorte in Linz and a chocolate gugelhupf cake for a bunch of bikers from Huddersfield. Along the way, they also meet a former baking world champion to see how he has reinvented gingerbread, and discover the 'green gold' of Austria - nutritious, delicious pumpkin seed oil. In this largely Catholic country, the Bikers overnight in a monastery and are up with the lark to cook kipferl, a giant 'brioche meets croissant', for the monks' breakfast. And, of course, you can't travel through Austria without learning to yodel. That is where Fritz comes in, mountain man, wood-fire cook and yodel coach - a real one-off.

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Shipbourne Farmers Market in Kent is a vital shop window for self-taught local farmers Carla and Robin, who use the milk from the family dairy herd to produce their own cheese. Since starting 15 years ago, they have become completely carbon neutral and have also picked up lots of awards for their cheese. Today at the market, Carla is looking to make plenty of sales. Meanwhile, Kent fruit farmer Tom helps run the family business and is keen to carry on his grandfather’s work promoting the home-grown Kent cobnut. As a local, Shipbourne Farmers Market holds a lot of childhood memories for him. However, today he is hoping for a windfall of fruit sales and that customers will be interested in bagging some of his new cobnut granola.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: David Attenborough reveals the life of the hippopotamus as never seen before. With incredible underwater footage, this film delves into the world of the hippo – an animal that cannot swim yet is utterly dependent on water. In Botswana's Okavango delta, hippos face an unparalleled challenge - deep floodwaters dry to dust in a matter of months. In one extraordinary season, the team go beneath the surface to see them protect their families and face their enemies as they deal with the drought. Going far beyond their dangerous reputation, the show discovers the true nature of the hippo, an animal that is compassionate, sensitive and highly intelligent.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: A collection of the best finds from the show's travels around the country, visiting Lulworth Castle in Dorset, Chiddingstone Castle in Kent and Wrest Park, Bedfordshire. The antiques experts include Christina Trevanion, Adam Partridge, Anita Manning, Thomas Plant, Mark Stacey and Catherine Southon - with items ranging from a fantastic collection of tin plate toys to an early camera. Paul Martin goes on a tour of the National Motor Museum at Beaulieu in Hampshire.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Karen Hauer, Storm Huntley, Joe Marler and Tom Read Wilson take on a series of rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games suitcase, or will they be tempted by the House of Games bee hotel?

programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: In Cardiff, Clive Myrie meets business owner Shalize, who wants to find a way to future-proof her health due to a family history of type 2 diabetes. Clive's suggestion is simple, powerful and time-efficient: press-ups! Do them regularly, and the science shows they could reduce the risk of diabetes, lower blood pressure and even help you live longer. A tiny habit with life-changing potential.

programme.title: Iolo's Anglesey
programme.desc: Iolo Williams explores the wildlife of Anglesey. Wales’s largest island is renowned for its coastal beauty, but it also has fantastic marshland and heathland with spectacular wildlife. Iolo watches breeding marsh harriers - majestic birds of prey that have only recently started to nest in Wales. He finds stoats, grey seals and lizards. He also visits Puffin Island to find the only breeding site in Wales for eider ducks. On a disused railway line, he finds breeding adders.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Gardening is all about looking ahead, and in that spirit, the Beechgrove Garden team are planning for winter. Ruth Vichos demonstrates how to cultivate and multiply snowdrops, and Calum Clunie collects seeds from this year’s lupins to sow for future colour. Calum also gets his feet wet as he looks at what you should be doing about pond maintenance right now. Ruth is in her strawberry bed discussing how you should be getting the most from your crop, and she also profiles some the country’s favourite garden plants in her competition plot. There is a visit to a fabulous garden in Orkney, along with all the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: As summer reaches its peak, Monty plans ahead, and after weeks of soaring temperatures, he’s got his work cut out refreshing the borders with a selection of late-summer perennials. He also has a rambling rose to tackle, and in the veg garden, the cleared beds are quickly being re-sown with crops for future harvests. Thirty years after the death of gardening legend Geoff Hamilton, Adam Frost makes a deeply personal visit to Barnsdale and reflects on the man whose huge influence helped shape both his career and love of horticulture. Carol Klein continues her fascinating journey into the secret life of plants. Exploring cutting-edge science, she discovers how vast networks of underground microbes work in partnership with plant roots, revealing the extraordinary hidden world beneath the earth. There’s an award-winning grower whose passion for gladioli has led to a collection of more than 1,800 spectacular blooms. Plus a visit to a remarkable Balinese-inspired tropical paradise nestled on the edge of the Brecon Beacons.

programme.title: Bergerac
programme.desc: With the team building a case against Mia and Tomos, Bergerac has to team up with his mother-in-law, Charlie, after discovering a new lead that takes him into the heart of the Jersey elite. Bergerac must use all of his fabled skills as a detective to tackle a new suspect that could blow the whole case wide open. But just as he seems to be making progress, a dangerous and unholy alliance is formed against him.

programme.title: QI XL
programme.desc: Sandi has a testing time with Susan Calman, Maisie Adam, Josh Widdicombe and Alan Davies.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Paddy O'Connell.

programme.title: Chuck Chuck Baby
programme.desc: Helen lives with her ex-husband and his 20-year-old girlfriend. Toiling at the local chicken factory and caring for Gwen, her much-loved mother-in-law, she lives by the clock. Her life is about to be turned upside down with the arrival back in town of Joanne, a carefree soul who she has not seen since her school days.

programme.title: Golf: Women's Open
programme.desc: Highlights of the second day of the Women’s Open from Royal Lytham & St Annes. South Korea’s Haeran Ryu is going for a third consecutive major victory, with American world number one Nelly Korda also looking to make it a hat-trick of major wins this season. England’s Georgia Hall returns to the scene of her famous win in 2018, with world number five Lottie Woad and world number seven Charlie Hull also on home soil looking to land their first major titles. Japan’s Miyu Yamashita defends the trophy she won at Royal Porthcawl in 2025.
