Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games suitcase, or will they be tempted by the House of Games bee hotel?

programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: In Cardiff, Clive Myrie meets business owner Shalize, who wants to find a way to future-proof her health due to a family history of type 2 diabetes. Clive's suggestion is simple, powerful and time-efficient: press-ups! Do them regularly, and the science shows they could reduce the risk of diabetes, lower blood pressure and even help you live longer. A tiny habit with life-changing potential.

programme.title: Iolo's Anglesey
programme.desc: Iolo Williams explores the wildlife of Anglesey. Wales’s largest island is renowned for its coastal beauty, but it also has fantastic marshland and heathland with spectacular wildlife. Iolo watches breeding marsh harriers - majestic birds of prey that have only recently started to nest in Wales. He finds stoats, grey seals and lizards. He also visits Puffin Island to find the only breeding site in Wales for eider ducks. On a disused railway line, he finds breeding adders.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Gardening is all about looking ahead, and in that spirit, the Beechgrove Garden team are planning for winter. Ruth Vichos demonstrates how to cultivate and multiply snowdrops, and Calum Clunie collects seeds from this year’s lupins to sow for future colour. Calum also gets his feet wet as he looks at what you should be doing about pond maintenance right now. Ruth is in her strawberry bed discussing how you should be getting the most from your crop, and she also profiles some the country’s favourite garden plants in her competition plot. There is a visit to a fabulous garden in Orkney, along with all the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: As summer reaches its peak, Monty plans ahead, and after weeks of soaring temperatures, he’s got his work cut out refreshing the borders with a selection of late-summer perennials. He also has a rambling rose to tackle, and in the veg garden, the cleared beds are quickly being re-sown with crops for future harvests. Thirty years after the death of gardening legend Geoff Hamilton, Adam Frost makes a deeply personal visit to Barnsdale and reflects on the man whose huge influence helped shape both his career and love of horticulture. Carol Klein continues her fascinating journey into the secret life of plants. Exploring cutting-edge science, she discovers how vast networks of underground microbes work in partnership with plant roots, revealing the extraordinary hidden world beneath the earth. There’s an award-winning grower whose passion for gladioli has led to a collection of more than 1,800 spectacular blooms. Plus a visit to a remarkable Balinese-inspired tropical paradise nestled on the edge of the Brecon Beacons.

programme.title: Bergerac
programme.desc: With the team building a case against Mia and Tomos, Bergerac has to team up with his mother-in-law, Charlie, after discovering a new lead that takes him into the heart of the Jersey elite. Bergerac must use all of his fabled skills as a detective to tackle a new suspect that could blow the whole case wide open. But just as he seems to be making progress, a dangerous and unholy alliance is formed against him.

programme.title: Spotlight
programme.desc: MI5 and police spent years snooping through the phone records of journalist Vincent Kearney, trying to find out who was giving him sensitive information. After those security services admitted the surveillance was unlawful and paid damages, Julian O’Neill investigates what they were up to, why they were in breach of the law and, crucially, why this case of state agencies spying on a journalist may not be an isolated example.

programme.title: Chronicles of the Sperrins
programme.desc: Sean and his guide dog Bennie climb Bessy Bell, taking in such treasures of the landscape as the holy well, the waters of which Sean believes has ‘the cure’.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Paddy O'Connell.

programme.title: Chuck Chuck Baby
programme.desc: Helen lives with her ex-husband and his 20-year-old girlfriend. Toiling at the local chicken factory and caring for Gwen, her much-loved mother-in-law, she lives by the clock. Her life is about to be turned upside down with the arrival back in town of Joanne, a carefree soul who she has not seen since her school days.

programme.title: Golf: Women's Open
programme.desc: Highlights of the second day of the Women’s Open from Royal Lytham & St Annes. South Korea’s Haeran Ryu is going for a third consecutive major victory, with American world number one Nelly Korda also looking to make it a hat-trick of major wins this season. England’s Georgia Hall returns to the scene of her famous win in 2018, with world number five Lottie Woad and world number seven Charlie Hull also on home soil looking to land their first major titles. Japan’s Miyu Yamashita defends the trophy she won at Royal Porthcawl in 2025.

programme.title: Ambulance
programme.desc: Critical care paramedic Matt administers pain relief to patient Neil before he is rushed to hospital, where doctors will assess him for suspected head and neck injuries.

programme.title: Evolution
programme.desc: How did the ostrich come to lay the biggest egg on earth? Chris Packham explores the way reproduction has shaped life on earth and the surprising evolutionary origins of sex, eggs and birds. It's a four-billion-year journey contained within a shell.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Sarah Moore leaves no stone unturned at Keynsham recycling centre in Somerset as she searches for three items with the potential to be repurposed or restored. A bucket of old toys has designer Rupert all revved up, but will his plan veer right off the road? Meanwhile, audio engineer Horse tries to retune a vintage TV for the modern market.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing Simply Provence
programme.desc: Marcus is visiting a local farmers' market, where each week a local French chef impresses the crowds with a live cooking demo. However, he’s been told a British chef is cooking tonight, and that chef… is Marcus. Can he convince the locals that Brits know how to cook? Later, Marcus has a VIP guest coming for dinner, the mayor of St Remy’s sister, and he really wants to impress. As she is a bit of a history buff, he decides to do some research into the origins of some local produce to find culinary inspiration.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Lifeline
programme.desc: Eddie Marsan presents this month’s Lifeline appeal on behalf of Tourettes Action, a charity which provides support, information and advocacy to improve the lives of people living with Tourette syndrome and their families.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week the celebrity contestants Yasmine Akram, Cariad Lloyd, Geoff Norcott and Dennis Taylor take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quick-fire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games kitchen composter?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple - make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Hairy Bikers' Bakeation
programme.desc: The home of Mozart, The Sound of Music and Arnold Schwarzenegger provides the fifth leg of the Hairy Bikers' adventure. The trip starts in Vienna, patisserie capital of the world, and ends atop the spectacular Grossglockner Alpine pass, one of the world's most spectacular biking roads. In Vienna, Si and Dave unravel the mystery of the two competing sachertorte recipes and taste the latest version - sachertorte 'reloaded'. They make apfelstrudel with the owner of a roadside B&B, cook linzertorte in Linz and a chocolate gugelhupf cake for a bunch of bikers from Huddersfield. Along the way, they also meet a former baking world champion to see how he has reinvented gingerbread, and discover the 'green gold' of Austria - nutritious, delicious pumpkin seed oil. In this largely Catholic country, the Bikers overnight in a monastery and are up with the lark to cook kipferl, a giant 'brioche meets croissant', for the monks' breakfast. And, of course, you can't travel through Austria without learning to yodel. That is where Fritz comes in, mountain man, wood-fire cook and yodel coach - a real one-off.

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Shipbourne Farmers Market in Kent is a vital shop window for self-taught local farmers Carla and Robin, who use the milk from the family dairy herd to produce their own cheese. Since starting 15 years ago, they have become completely carbon neutral and have also picked up lots of awards for their cheese. Today at the market, Carla is looking to make plenty of sales. Meanwhile, Kent fruit farmer Tom helps run the family business and is keen to carry on his grandfather’s work promoting the home-grown Kent cobnut. As a local, Shipbourne Farmers Market holds a lot of childhood memories for him. However, today he is hoping for a windfall of fruit sales and that customers will be interested in bagging some of his new cobnut granola.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: David Attenborough reveals the life of the hippopotamus as never seen before. With incredible underwater footage, this film delves into the world of the hippo – an animal that cannot swim yet is utterly dependent on water. In Botswana's Okavango delta, hippos face an unparalleled challenge - deep floodwaters dry to dust in a matter of months. In one extraordinary season, the team go beneath the surface to see them protect their families and face their enemies as they deal with the drought. Going far beyond their dangerous reputation, the show discovers the true nature of the hippo, an animal that is compassionate, sensitive and highly intelligent.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: A collection of the best finds from the show's travels around the country, visiting Lulworth Castle in Dorset, Chiddingstone Castle in Kent and Wrest Park, Bedfordshire. The antiques experts include Christina Trevanion, Adam Partridge, Anita Manning, Thomas Plant, Mark Stacey and Catherine Southon - with items ranging from a fantastic collection of tin plate toys to an early camera. Paul Martin goes on a tour of the National Motor Museum at Beaulieu in Hampshire.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple - make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Hairy Bikers' Bakeation
programme.desc: The home of Mozart, The Sound of Music and Arnold Schwarzenegger provides the fifth leg of the Hairy Bikers' adventure. The trip starts in Vienna, patisserie capital of the world, and ends atop the spectacular Grossglockner Alpine pass, one of the world's most spectacular biking roads. In Vienna, Si and Dave unravel the mystery of the two competing sachertorte recipes and taste the latest version - sachertorte 'reloaded'. They make apfelstrudel with the owner of a roadside B&B, cook linzertorte in Linz and a chocolate gugelhupf cake for a bunch of bikers from Huddersfield. Along the way, they also meet a former baking world champion to see how he has reinvented gingerbread, and discover the 'green gold' of Austria - nutritious, delicious pumpkin seed oil. In this largely Catholic country, the Bikers overnight in a monastery and are up with the lark to cook kipferl, a giant 'brioche meets croissant', for the monks' breakfast. And, of course, you can't travel through Austria without learning to yodel. That is where Fritz comes in, mountain man, wood-fire cook and yodel coach - a real one-off.

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Shipbourne Farmers Market in Kent is a vital shop window for self-taught local farmers Carla and Robin, who use the milk from the family dairy herd to produce their own cheese. Since starting 15 years ago, they have become completely carbon neutral and have also picked up lots of awards for their cheese. Today at the market, Carla is looking to make plenty of sales. Meanwhile, Kent fruit farmer Tom helps run the family business and is keen to carry on his grandfather’s work promoting the home-grown Kent cobnut. As a local, Shipbourne Farmers Market holds a lot of childhood memories for him. However, today he is hoping for a windfall of fruit sales and that customers will be interested in bagging some of his new cobnut granola.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: David Attenborough reveals the life of the hippopotamus as never seen before. With incredible underwater footage, this film delves into the world of the hippo – an animal that cannot swim yet is utterly dependent on water. In Botswana's Okavango delta, hippos face an unparalleled challenge - deep floodwaters dry to dust in a matter of months. In one extraordinary season, the team go beneath the surface to see them protect their families and face their enemies as they deal with the drought. Going far beyond their dangerous reputation, the show discovers the true nature of the hippo, an animal that is compassionate, sensitive and highly intelligent.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: A collection of the best finds from the show's travels around the country, visiting Lulworth Castle in Dorset, Chiddingstone Castle in Kent and Wrest Park, Bedfordshire. The antiques experts include Christina Trevanion, Adam Partridge, Anita Manning, Thomas Plant, Mark Stacey and Catherine Southon - with items ranging from a fantastic collection of tin plate toys to an early camera. Paul Martin goes on a tour of the National Motor Museum at Beaulieu in Hampshire.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Karen Hauer, Storm Huntley, Joe Marler and Tom Read Wilson take on a series of rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games suitcase, or will they be tempted by the House of Games bee hotel?

programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: In Cardiff, Clive Myrie meets business owner Shalize, who wants to find a way to future-proof her health due to a family history of type 2 diabetes. Clive's suggestion is simple, powerful and time-efficient: press-ups! Do them regularly, and the science shows they could reduce the risk of diabetes, lower blood pressure and even help you live longer. A tiny habit with life-changing potential.

programme.title: Iolo's Anglesey
programme.desc: Iolo Williams explores the wildlife of Anglesey. Wales’s largest island is renowned for its coastal beauty, but it also has fantastic marshland and heathland with spectacular wildlife. Iolo watches breeding marsh harriers - majestic birds of prey that have only recently started to nest in Wales. He finds stoats, grey seals and lizards. He also visits Puffin Island to find the only breeding site in Wales for eider ducks. On a disused railway line, he finds breeding adders.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Gardening is all about looking ahead, and in that spirit, the Beechgrove Garden team are planning for winter. Ruth Vichos demonstrates how to cultivate and multiply snowdrops, and Calum Clunie collects seeds from this year’s lupins to sow for future colour. Calum also gets his feet wet as he looks at what you should be doing about pond maintenance right now. Ruth is in her strawberry bed discussing how you should be getting the most from your crop, and she also profiles some the country’s favourite garden plants in her competition plot. There is a visit to a fabulous garden in Orkney, along with all the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: As summer reaches its peak, Monty plans ahead, and after weeks of soaring temperatures, he’s got his work cut out refreshing the borders with a selection of late-summer perennials. He also has a rambling rose to tackle, and in the veg garden, the cleared beds are quickly being re-sown with crops for future harvests. Thirty years after the death of gardening legend Geoff Hamilton, Adam Frost makes a deeply personal visit to Barnsdale and reflects on the man whose huge influence helped shape both his career and love of horticulture. Carol Klein continues her fascinating journey into the secret life of plants. Exploring cutting-edge science, she discovers how vast networks of underground microbes work in partnership with plant roots, revealing the extraordinary hidden world beneath the earth. There’s an award-winning grower whose passion for gladioli has led to a collection of more than 1,800 spectacular blooms. Plus a visit to a remarkable Balinese-inspired tropical paradise nestled on the edge of the Brecon Beacons.

programme.title: Bergerac
programme.desc: With the team building a case against Mia and Tomos, Bergerac has to team up with his mother-in-law, Charlie, after discovering a new lead that takes him into the heart of the Jersey elite. Bergerac must use all of his fabled skills as a detective to tackle a new suspect that could blow the whole case wide open. But just as he seems to be making progress, a dangerous and unholy alliance is formed against him.

programme.title: Chuck Chuck Baby
programme.desc: Helen lives with her ex-husband and his 20-year-old girlfriend. Toiling at the local chicken factory and caring for Gwen, her much-loved mother-in-law, she lives by the clock. Her life is about to be turned upside down with the arrival back in town of Joanne, a carefree soul who she has not seen since her school days.

programme.title: Golf: Women's Open
programme.desc: Highlights of the second day of the Women’s Open from Royal Lytham & St Annes. South Korea’s Haeran Ryu is going for a third consecutive major victory, with American world number one Nelly Korda also looking to make it a hat-trick of major wins this season. England’s Georgia Hall returns to the scene of her famous win in 2018, with world number five Lottie Woad and world number seven Charlie Hull also on home soil looking to land their first major titles. Japan’s Miyu Yamashita defends the trophy she won at Royal Porthcawl in 2025.

Mum decides to put Triggs's beloved but smelly, squeaky teddy in the washing machine, but Triggs is terrified Teddy will be lost forever. Maddie must win his trust, because that teddy really stinks!

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: Shooting stars are flying over Flat Top Mountain. Everyone in Fine Forest climbs the mountain, except Fiona, who has hurt her foot! The Piggies can’t leave her behind. Will a rocket do the trick?

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos are in a hairdresser's salon. They watch as the hairdresser puts all his signs outside the shop. Whilst the hairdresser is busy, the Twirlywoos decide to put everything outside... including the customers! The Fruit Tea Machine has gone wrong. The tube has gone up so high that it has opened the top of the Big Red Boat and the spout is outside by the Quacky Birds. The Twirlywoos are struggling to pump the tea up to the top of the tube. The Quacky Birds jump up and down on the orange at the top of the tube, but they can only manage to get drips out. The Hooter comes to the rescue and the fruit tea pours from outside the Big Red Boat into the teapot.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Fishy fun with Justin and his friends as they visit an aquarium and meet a diver. Meanwhile, Mr Tumble in on the hunt for some underwater treasure!

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: A red balloon floats into Teletubbyland and Po leads the tubby phone dance in a special episode about Po's favourite colour. Po shows the Tiddlytubbies the red balloon and all of the Teletubbies watch children play in a room full of red balloons.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Nigel and Baby Bear welcome babies Layla, Betsy, Tobias, Amelia, Amber, Ferne, Ezra and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Inside everyone’s bags in this episode are Sticks which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding safe, baby appropriate sticks inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The fun rhyme ‘One, Two, Buckle My Shoe’ features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Action Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: In Tall Trees Forest, Lisa and the children have bubbly fun washing toy clothes, learning British Sign Language signs for jungle, clothes and washing, then they sing and sign Down in the Jungle.

programme.title: I Can Grow It
programme.desc: Aaron, Mia and Joda explore herbs in the city garden, smelling, touching and tasting them while learning about the joy and magic they bring to the garden.

programme.title: Hamza Loves Animals: Africa
programme.desc: Kipekee the baby elephant is fed up with being small. Hamza finds some wonderful wildebeest in the wild. Later, he uses a brush to help the baby rhinos relax.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Lou’s trunk won’t wake up until Kiri finds a chilly solution.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey's having fun copying everything Dad says and does, but the game takes a serious turn when Bluey finds a hurt budgie and they have to make an emergency trip to the vet.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee is cleaning the clubhouse, so the Squirrels take refuge in the treehouse, but it's getting a little bit cramped these days. Norrie has an idea - maybe they need to add an extension, just like her dad does when she gets new siblings.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: It’s the return of the Sorting Express, and Lime’s friends use it to help sort colours for her concert.

programme.title: Teeny Tiny Creatures
programme.desc: Harriet wants to find out all about blue tits in today’s episode. Chantelle visits a school and discovers that they have a bird box which is currently home to a family of blue tits, whilst Rory meet a young birdwatcher in her garden. Chantelle and Rory’s fact files help answer all of Harriet’s questions. With the help of the Teeny Tiny Creatures poem we discover that, like lots of other teeny tiny creatures, blue tits are superheroes and help our planet in their own special way. In the Teeny Tiny Task, Chantelle and the children make blue tit masks and have fun flying around the school grounds.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Ted has big plans for his sister Sofia’s birthday. He organises a family tea party and begins by making delicious cupcakes. He also plans a scavenger hunt in the garden as a surprise. But will Sofia find all the hidden presents? Later, Ted’s cousins arrive to join in the fun and the family guinea pigs don’t miss out on the partying either!

programme.title: Big Cook Little Cook
programme.desc: Children’s cookery series with Big Cook Jen and Little Cook Small. Small wants to be the first at everything in the cafe, including greeting today's customer Bounce the Bunny. Jen and Small decide to make Bounce a rabbity carrot cake.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Newfoundland Sylvie is a therapy dog with big soft cuddles who loves to help people when they’re worried. She and her owner Katrina visit all sorts of people every day, young and old. It’s Sylvie and Katrina’s day off, and they’re planning a special lunch at the park café. At the bus stop, they meet Dawn from the toy shop, who is worried that her bus is running late. But seeing Sylvie waiting calmly inspires Dawn to do the same. At the park, Katrina and Sylvie bump into Harry the baker, literally! Harry is worried too; his shop oven isn’t working. Sylvie nuzzles him in support. Grateful for their help, Harry offers Sylvie and Katrina a cake. Then, they meet Pete the postie, who is helping his daughter Caitlin ride her balance bike for the first time. Katrina suggests that Sylvie walks alongside Caitlin as she finds her confidence. Before long, Caitlin is loving every moment. Katrina and Sylvie finally arrive at the park café, only to find that it’s closed. Sylvie summons her super heart and the friends they’ve met along the way to comfort Katrina and to show her that when you’re kind to others, they’re often kind to you in return.

programme.title: Time for School
programme.desc: Mrs Farrell and the children create a class charter – a list of rules to follow to all get along with one another at school. The class put the rules into practice by sharing together and being kind to each other. Ottilie and Felicity find out how to look after the giant African land snails. Leon takes charge of keeping the classroom tidy and ends up being awarded a certificate for all his hard work.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Baba can't wait for his swimming lesson, and he has a great instructor - his big sister. Oona teaches Baba to paddle, steer with his feet and put his head under the water. With some practice and encouragement from Oona and Mama, Baba starts to get the hang of it - but diving proves much more difficult, until Lala drops a shiny shell in the water.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: A samba band is coming to play, and everyone is helping to prepare. Stripes is so busy that he has forgotten one thing - to book the band! With no band coming, all seems lost, until Yukee and Stripes realise the Sunhouse already has its own brilliant band!

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Everyone is excited to see the new piece of pottery that Mum has made - it's a glug jug! But when Maddie accidentally breaks a piece of the jug, she doesn't know what to do. Should she try to cover it up, or should she just tell mum?

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: Keith wants to have a pirate adventure, so the Piggies build him a wheeled ship. Together, they sail across Fine Forest in search of treasure. When Wilf hears about their hunt, he joins the crew. But he only has one thing in mind... to steal the treasure!

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: When their numberlings fall off, the Numberblocks have to work out who they are and how numbers work. Learn about place value with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: CH and SH go head to head in the Alphablocks Games and pit a ship and a shop against a chip and a chop. This episode has fun with the '-ch-' and '-sh-' digraphs and the words shop, chop, chip, ship, shin, chin, shed, mash, cash and sash.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Educational series using Makaton sign language. Mr Tumble visits Baker Tumble's bakery, while Justin spends the day with two best friends who love to bake cakes together.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: The Teletubbies count to four - four Teletubbies, four flowers, four pieces of tubby toast. In Tummy Tales, two sisters help their dad put a number four on the front door of their house.

programme.title: Andy's Prehistoric Adventures
programme.desc: Andy travels back 70 million years to meet the miniature magyarosaurus, a relative of the giant sauropod dinosaurs, which grew no bigger than a pony. But when he arrives on their prehistoric island home, he has to shrink down as well to hide from a giant flying reptile as tall as a giraffe.

programme.title: Molly and Mack
programme.desc: Molly examines her shelf of special things at the back of Mack’s stall. She chooses the sprig of lavender and remembers the day she got it… Molly feels sad. Everything reminds her of Alice today, including James’s book, Ruby’s origami and Bob’s lavender. James and Ruby think of ways to cheer her up. Ruby suggests Molly should make a fairy bundle with Bob’s lavender. Mrs Juniper decides to make pesto pasta from Bob’s bumper basil crop as a lunchtime special. Moira turns her nose up at it, telling Mrs Juniper that she doesn’t like pesto. At lunch, Mrs Juniper decides to test out Moira’s stubbornness by sneaking some into her plain chicken sandwich.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: In this episode, CBeebies’ very own motorbike rider Grace shows off three amazing machines that were made to help people in emergencies. Grace puts out a real fire in an airport fire engine, shows off amazing search-and-rescue helicopters, and drives an ambulance.

programme.title: Dodge's Pup School
programme.desc: Everyone's excited about the scavenger hunt around the school playground, until they discover Miss Collie has mixed up the pups' usual working groups. Dodge misses working with his best friends, Jazz and Woofer. He must learn to work with his partner, Tiny, instead. The two pups discover they can work together - and have a lot of fun along the way!

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: A young Cornasaurolophus starts popping, which draws the attention of the Bananaraptors!

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: The Octonauts must clear a logjam while protecting a family of birds.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Peter accidentally destroys the squirrels' store of nuts with one of Mr Bouncer's misfiring inventions, he sets off to perilous Owl Island to replace them!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Join Duggee, a big, lovable dog, as he runs the Squirrel Club, where children can earn badges for learning new skills. Warm-hearted preschool series about trying new things.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: When Zigzag loses books all over Sweetwood, Vida comes up with a way to find them.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: It’s Evil Pea’s birthday, but she and Carrot are trapped in the bottom of her freezer. They must put their differences aside and work together to escape.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: Weasy and the Ducklings find a chest full of circus supplies. When the cheeky Chipmunk puts on his own show, Weasy trains the Ducklings to do an incredible circus act that will impress the whole farm!

programme.title: Do Not Watch This Show
programme.desc: It's a smelly disaster - the longer you stay tuned, the worse everything stinks!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Indy’s upset her model horse looks like a cow, but Calypso encourages her not to give up.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey must find a way to play postman and the ground's lava without squabbling with Bingo.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Boom is showing off but slips and has a mild panic. To hide his embarrassment, he challenges Zog to a dragon-off! Zog must set aside his desire to win and help his rival.

programme.title: Andy's Dino Island
programme.desc: Andy and Jen are on an epic adventure to discover what the dinosaurs of Dino Island get up to at night. When Andy loses his gizmo and gets lost in the dark, a friendly velociraptor comes to his aid. Along the way, Andy spots a T rex and narrowly avoids being stomped on by a herd of Alamosaurus, who are protecting their eggs.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle learns that the summer holidays will soon be over and Evie will be going to school. Determined not to be left alone, Waffle hatches a plan to keep the family at home.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: It’s raining, so Rafi and Ruby are playing indoor football. But when they accidentally break a plate, Rafi wishes for it to be fixed but warns them not to play again. When the plate smashes a second time, Rafi wishes for help and summons the clumsy Fixie Pixie, who causes chaos while trying to repair things. Rafi eventually realises it’s better to tell the truth than hide mistakes.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo and her family are ready for an exciting day on the beach playing cricket, but Auntie Dee hasn't packed the wickets! Luckily, Gran Gran has a plan to use things on the beach to make new wickets. Everyone has so much fun playing, but who will win?

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Scarf Lady's old film reels get themselves in a tangle, so Sarah and Duck decide to recreate the footage.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: A robot like a camera on wheels lands on the planet, flashing, bleeping and taking photos. At first the Clangers are scared of it but as they begin to accept it, they find it has a lot to show them about the universe and everywhere it has been.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa tidy up some colourful balls but can’t find the right home for a squishy ball. They bring the ball to the Play Tree and play with a shape sorter. The squishy ball gets stuck inside, and the shapes won’t fit. In Yummy Land, when there aren’t enough seats at the table, MeMo uses the squishy ball as a seat. At BeddyByes time, Gramma Leeba finds the perfect home for the squishy ball.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: A mysterious jet of water, a tiddle, appears suddenly next to Igglepiggle. He discovers that he can control it by stamping his feet. Delighted, he takes it to Makka Pakka, who finds it very useful indeed.

programme.title: CBeebies Bedtime Stories
programme.desc: Blue Peter presenters Abby, Shini, Joel and Hacker read the classic story of one caterpillar with a huge appetite.

programme.title: This Is CBeebies
programme.desc: Programmes start at 6.00am.

programme.title: The Summit
programme.desc: Ben Shephard presents the first episode of a thrilling reality series as 14 ordinary Brits set off to climb one of New Zealand's highest peaks to win a share of 200,000 pounds - with their progress tracked by the menacing Mountain's Keeper, they have just 14 days to make the 100-kilometre journey across treacherous terrain and perilous crossings. However, not everyone can make it to The Summit as the group face vote-offs at each base camp along the way, and they come across terrifying crossings as they set off on their hike. Pub landlady Miranda must face her fears and prove that she is not slowing the group down, while self-styled 'shark' Dockers singles out his competition and makes an early bid to be a leader. The Mountain's Keeper then tests the group's resolve to get to The Summit by forcing them to make a brutal decision, causing tensions to boil over in a dramatic fallout and leave the team divided.

programme.title: The Summit
programme.desc: Ben Shephard presents the first episode of a thrilling reality series as 14 ordinary Brits set off to climb one of New Zealand's highest peaks to win a share of 200,000 pounds - with their progress tracked by the menacing Mountain's Keeper, they have just 14 days to make the 100-kilometre journey across treacherous terrain and perilous crossings. However, not everyone can make it to The Summit as the group face vote-offs at each base camp along the way, and they come across terrifying crossings as they set off on their hike. Pub landlady Miranda must face her fears and prove that she is not slowing the group down, while self-styled 'shark' Dockers singles out his competition and makes an early bid to be a leader. The Mountain's Keeper then tests the group's resolve to get to The Summit by forcing them to make a brutal decision, causing tensions to boil over in a dramatic fallout and leave the team divided.

programme.title: The Summit
programme.desc: Ben Shephard presents the first episode of a thrilling reality series as 14 ordinary Brits set off to climb one of New Zealand's highest peaks to win a share of 200,000 pounds - with their progress tracked by the menacing Mountain's Keeper, they have just 14 days to make the 100-kilometre journey across treacherous terrain and perilous crossings. However, not everyone can make it to The Summit as the group face vote-offs at each base camp along the way, and they come across terrifying crossings as they set off on their hike. Pub landlady Miranda must face her fears and prove that she is not slowing the group down, while self-styled 'shark' Dockers singles out his competition and makes an early bid to be a leader. The Mountain's Keeper then tests the group's resolve to get to The Summit by forcing them to make a brutal decision, causing tensions to boil over in a dramatic fallout and leave the team divided.

programme.title: The Summit
programme.desc: Ben Shephard presents the first episode of a thrilling reality series as 14 ordinary Brits set off to climb one of New Zealand's highest peaks to win a share of 200,000 pounds - with their progress tracked by the menacing Mountain's Keeper, they have just 14 days to make the 100-kilometre journey across treacherous terrain and perilous crossings. However, not everyone can make it to The Summit as the group face vote-offs at each base camp along the way, and they come across terrifying crossings as they set off on their hike. Pub landlady Miranda must face her fears and prove that she is not slowing the group down, while self-styled 'shark' Dockers singles out his competition and makes an early bid to be a leader. The Mountain's Keeper then tests the group's resolve to get to The Summit by forcing them to make a brutal decision, causing tensions to boil over in a dramatic fallout and leave the team divided.

programme.title: The Summit
programme.desc: Ben Shephard presents the first episode of a thrilling reality series as 14 ordinary Brits set off to climb one of New Zealand's highest peaks to win a share of 200,000 pounds - with their progress tracked by the menacing Mountain's Keeper, they have just 14 days to make the 100-kilometre journey across treacherous terrain and perilous crossings. However, not everyone can make it to The Summit as the group face vote-offs at each base camp along the way, and they come across terrifying crossings as they set off on their hike. Pub landlady Miranda must face her fears and prove that she is not slowing the group down, while self-styled 'shark' Dockers singles out his competition and makes an early bid to be a leader. The Mountain's Keeper then tests the group's resolve to get to The Summit by forcing them to make a brutal decision, causing tensions to boil over in a dramatic fallout and leave the team divided.

programme.title: The Only Way is Essex
programme.desc: The gang are going out with a bang as Chloe S, TOWIE's Queen of Essex, is turning 40, and throwing a birthday gala to celebrate. Taking their inspiration from Hollywood's elite, there'll be enviable glamour and glitz galore at this swanky soiree... and drama of epic proportions. Will he be able to pull out all the stops and make it up to her with a gift that she'll never forget? When Pete's away, Diags will play and give Chloe the best send-off to her 30s via her very own Chloe-inspired awards ceremony. As all her friends and family gather to show just how much she means to them, will she be able to make it through the night without a tear? Meanwhile, quiet boy Roman remains quiet no more - he's had enough of holding onto other people's secrets and decides that a birthday party is the best time to gift Dani and Gatsby some home truths about their relationship.

programme.title: Grantchester

As he struggles to remember her final words, Geordie grows concerned both for the murdered girl - who was so callously abandoned outside a local slum - and for his friend's troubled state of mind. Once at the slum, Sidney and Geordie identify the girl as Sadie Parker and meet her shocked roommates Ava, Lottie and Peggy - although they claim to be seamstresses, Geordie realises that they are involved in a life of vice while Sidney finds his missing jacket in Sadie's room and realises that he gave it to her the night before. When the pair track down Mr Simpson, the owner and employer of the girls who is playing golf with councilman Archer Davis, Sidney's frustrations with his own failings bubbles over into an angry confrontation with Simpson...
